analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Sunday Sky's Rendering as a Service (RAS) architecture. The rendering process begins when client devices request personalized videos through API Gateway, which controls load using usage plans and API keys. API Gateway forwards requests to the RAS Frontend Lambda function, which validates rendering requests and places rendering instructions onto an SQS Jobs Queue. Spot-backed rendering EC2 instances inside an Auto Scaling Group poll the SQS Jobs Queue for work. Upon taking a job, the EC2 instance immediately responds to an SQS Responses Queue, which the RAS Frontend Lambda polls to return a playlist link back to the client device. Finished video segments are uploaded directly by rendering EC2 instances to an S3 Bucket, which CloudFront streams to the client device. For scaling, EC2 instances push custom performance metrics to CloudWatch, and a Step Functions workflow triggers a Scaling Lambda every 15 seconds to evaluate load and instruct the Auto Scaling Group to adjust capacity. For spot interruption handling, CloudWatch Events notifies an Interruption Handler Lambda when a spot instance is marked for termination. The Lambda makes an API call to the specific EC2 instance to stop pulling jobs and drain current tasks, then detaches the instance from the Auto Scaling Group.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates the modernization of an independent insurance agent application for Main Street America (part of American Family Group). Agents access a single-page frontend served via CloudFront from S3. API calls are sent via CloudFront to API Gateway, which triggers a Lambda Authorizer to validate user access. Authorized API requests are processed by a serverless Python Lambda function. As part of a strangler pattern modernization, functionality not yet migrated to Lambda is delegated to legacy Tomcat servers on EC2, which respond back to Lambda. Lambda also caches regional user session state in DynamoDB for fast cross-AZ availability.

graph.name: American Family Group - Main Street America App Modernization
graph.notes: Architecture demonstrating incremental strangler-pattern serverless modernization using CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, and legacy Tomcat on EC2.

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Marathon Oil's serverless pipeline for processing drone imagery of well pads. Drones upload flight images to a 3rd Party Software. A scheduled CloudWatch Event triggers a Step Functions workflow that orchestrates three Lambda functions. The first Lambda function polls the 3rd Party Software API for new images. The 3rd party software copies images to an S3 bucket. A Lambda function creates raster proxies and saves metadata into an On-Prem Database. On-Prem Servers running mapping software access the drone imagery in S3 via Storage Gateway using these raster proxy identifiers. All components are mapped according to exact visual and verbal transcript descriptions.
